page: Amazon Web Services t4g.2xlarge is an arm64 burstable instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Provisioned on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance supplies 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a single thread per core topology. Hardware resources include 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per core, backed by 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance features a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, does not include local disk storage, and contains no hardware graphics accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight balanced multi-core efficiency alongside restrained single-threaded execution. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved 1519.68 points on single-core tasks and 12133.02 points across all cores. Geekbench testing mirrors this separation with a single-core score of 877.0 and a multi-core score of 5149.0. Memory bandwidth remains steady under read operations at 114.09 GB/sec for uncached blocks, supporting strong throughput in Redis SET operations at 9.35 million operations per second and static web serving at 9.19 GB/sec. Conversely, compression workloads, single-threaded decompression, and text processing sit within the lower percentiles.

Cost efficiency for t4g.2xlarge is defined by its burstable allocation model, which utilizes CPU credits to accommodate spikes while maintaining lower operating resource overhead. Continuous heavy computation risks depleting credit balances and throttles core throughput to baseline levels. Furthermore, workloads requiring non-volatile storage must allocate network-attached block volumes due to the absence of bundled local disks. The instance is suited for variable-traffic web servers, caching nodes, asynchronous application queues, continuous integration builds, and containerized microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.2xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 8 physical cores, 8 vCPUs, and 32.0 GB of memory, it maintains a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio without multi-threading. The instance features a burstable CPU credit allocation running on the Nitro hypervisor, paired with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It does not provide bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs. Benchmark results place multi-core operations, software compilation, database tasks, and Redis throughput within average performance percentiles, reaching 9.35 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.19 GB/sec static web throughput. Conversely, single-threaded throughput, cryptographic operations, and compression remain weaker. Delivering efficient resource allocation for intermittent activity, t4g.2xlarge fits burstable microservices, development environments, CI/CD compilation tasks, caching layers, and web application serving with variable load profiles.
